chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

The waiting period of a woman who gives khula' (divorce by mutual consent) is forty-five days. This report carries two interpretations: one is that if the woman is a slave who does not menstruate, but a similar slave does menstruate, her waiting period is forty-five days when her husband grants her khula'. The other interpretation is that the report is specific to a woman whose habit is to menstruate three times within this period, which amounts to forty-five days. On both interpretations, it does not contradict the earlier reports.

key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَة: A woman who obtains divorce by paying compensation to her husband (khula)
key_terms.حِيَض: Plural of haidh, meaning menstrual periods
key_terms.عِدَّة: Waiting period observed by a woman after divorce or death of husband

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman who gives khula in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) to clarify the 'iddah of a mukhtali'ah (woman seeking khula'), proposing two scholarly interpretations: either it applies to a slave woman who does not menstruate, or it is specific to a woman whose three menstrual cycles fit within forty-five days. This dual approach ensures harmony with other primary narrations, reflecting the Shia juristic method of reconciling apparent textual discrepancies through contextual specification (takhsis).
